summary.headline: Utkarsh SFB narrowed Q1 FY27 net loss to INR34 crore (down over 80% YoY and QoQ), with GNPA at 5.9% and credit cost at 2.3%.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 showed a clear turn: total disbursements rose 49% YoY, fresh slippages fell to about INR125 crore from INR170 crore in Q4 FY26, and GNPA improved to 5.9% (about 550 bps YoY, 160 bps QoQ). Cost of funds fell to 7.7%, and PPOP rose to INR64 crore from INR12 crore in Q4. Profitability is not yet normal; the bank is still loss-making, and CGFMU guarantee benefit of about INR75 crore supported the P&L. Management guided to 25-30% loan growth, NIM around 8% and ROE around 15% by FY28, while analysts pressed on the quality of the legacy book and the growth push.

financial_highlights.metric: Fresh slippages (net of recoveries and upgradations)
financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR170 crore QoQ and ~INR400 crore YoY
vs 5.3% in Q4 FY26 and 8.5% in Q1 FY26
about fivefold vs INR12 crore in Q4 FY26
Micro Banking ~INR45 crore, non-Micro Banking ~INR64 crore

segments.name: Micro Banking (JLG + MBBL)
segments.commentary: JLG is 26% of gross loans (28% incl. BC JLG), down from 88% in March 2020. MBBL grew 147% YoY and 11% QoQ and is now above 30% of Micro Banking; Micro Banking slippages were INR68 crore vs INR153 crore in Q4, and Micro Banking SMA pools were 1.2%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR4,482 crore, up 12% YoY, with Micro LAP disbursement yield around 18%. GNPA about INR169 crore, or 3.8%.

segments.name: Housing / BBG / Gold / CV-CE
segments.commentary: Housing INR1,005 crore (up 8% YoY); BBG business banking up 40% YoY; gold loans about INR300 crore; used vehicles about 30% of CV/CE disbursements. Non-MFI GNPA about INR425 crore: MSME INR169 crore, CV&CE INR62 crore, WSL about INR30 crore, housing about INR49-50 crore.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Total deposits up 3% YoY; CASA up 15% and retail term deposits up 15% YoY. CASA ratio 22%, CASA plus retail TD 83% (vs 74% a year ago).

guidance_outlook: Loan book growth of 25-30% YoY (JLG and Micro Banking together 15-20%, JLG below 20%), with secured lending around 55% of portfolio.
NIM around 8%; ROE around 15% by FY28; management guided to a 2-digit ROE exiting FY27.
Credit cost guided at upper-end 3-3.5% going forward, described as conservative.
Tier 2 NCD raise of INR500 crore planned this year, expected to add about 250 bps to CRAR; no equity raise anticipated until at least end-FY27.
Early redemption of INR195 crore tranche at 12.5% coupon in mid-August, expected to save about INR20 crore.
Cost of funds to benefit further from progressive repricing over coming quarters.
NCLT hearing on the reverse merger of holding company UCL into the bank fixed for August 6, 2026; completion expected in the next few months, subject to NCLT.
Recoveries expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3 FY27, with about 1,100 JLG collection staff to be redeployed toward NPA recovery and write-offs.
capex_capacity: Around 1,100 branches; strategy is productivity over branch expansion. Headcount rationalised by about 1,700.
New LMS switchover completed; a new core banking system is about to launch; Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation under way.
Collections workforce for JLG and MBBL exceeds 1,200; JLG collection headcount about 1,100, with a specialised call centre for overdue accounts.
demand_pricing: Industry JLG portfolio reportedly down about 30%; management says it will grow JLG only in its core geography, using partners outside it.
MBBL disbursements are about 99.9% existing customers with 2-3 prior cycles; a small pilot is open to new-to-bank customers.
Retail term deposit card rates cut: senior citizen peak 9.1% now 8.25%; general citizen 8.5% now 8.1%.
Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 30% YoY; Q1 FY27 disbursements grew 49% YoY.
